evals.prompt: Find up to 3 apartments for rent in Al Narjis, Riyadh, with annual rent no more than SAR 60,000. Give me a concise Markdown comparison.
evals.expected_output: Runs structured Aqar and approximate Haraj searches, then presents Haraj and Aqar sections with at most three results per source and clear filter-fidelity notes.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/aqar.mjs" search` with city, district, rent purpose, apartment type, maximum price, limit 3, and `--json`.
Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/haraj.mjs" search` with a focused apartment-rental keyword, Riyadh, limit 3, and `--json`.
The response contains exactly two marketplace sections: `## Haraj` followed by `## Aqar`.
The response explains that Haraj did not enforce structured district, purpose, type, or maximum-price filters.
Each returned listing includes an ID, price when available, and canonical URL.

evals.prompt: Show me up to 5 villas for sale in Jeddah with at least 300 square meters and a maximum price of SAR 2 million.
evals.expected_output: Queries both marketplaces, uses Aqar's structured filters where supported, approximates the Haraj search, and discloses unsupported Haraj area and price constraints.
expectations: Both Aqar and Haraj bundled runner searches are evidenced, with `--limit 5` and `--json`.
The response contains exactly two marketplace sections: `## Haraj` followed by `## Aqar`.
The response explains that neither CLI has a structured area filter, that Aqar area may only be filtered from returned candidates, and that Haraj cannot enforce area from its normalized results.
The response does not claim that Haraj natively enforced maximum price.
No more than five listings appear in either marketplace section.

evals.prompt: Find up to 4 Toyota Camry ads in Riyadh posted during the last week.
evals.expected_output: Treats the vehicle request as non-real-estate and searches Haraj only.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/haraj.mjs" search` with a Camry keyword, Riyadh, `--during-date 1week`, `--limit 4`, and `--json`.
No Aqar command is invoked.
The response contains no Aqar results section.

evals.prompt: Compare three used RTX 4090 ads in Saudi Arabia.
evals.expected_output: Treats the electronics request as non-real-estate and searches Haraj only.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/haraj.mjs" search` with an RTX 4090 keyword, `--limit 3`, and `--json`.
No Aqar command is invoked.
Every presented result is attributable to Haraj and preserves its canonical URL.

evals.prompt: Find me two apartments for rent in Riyadh and two used Camrys in Riyadh.
evals.expected_output: Partitions the mixed request: searches both sources for apartments and Haraj only for cars.
expectations: Command evidence includes Aqar and Haraj property searches with limit 2.
Command evidence includes a separate Haraj Camry search with limit 2.
Aqar is not used for the vehicle portion.
The property results contain exactly two marketplace sections: `## Haraj` followed by `## Aqar`.

evals.prompt: Search Aqar only for three apartments for rent in Riyadh.
evals.expected_output: Honors the explicit source restriction and searches only Aqar.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/aqar.mjs" search` with rent and apartment filters, limit 3, and `--json`.
No Haraj command is invoked.
The response presents only Aqar results.

evals.prompt: Look up this property ad and summarize it: https://haraj.com.sa/11187108979/example/
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the Haraj URL and performs a source-specific Haraj detail lookup.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/haraj.mjs" get` with the URL or parsed listing ID and `--json`.
No Aqar command is invoked.
The response preserves the canonical Haraj URL and does not invent missing property fields.

evals.prompt: Get property listing 6736135 and show me its details.
evals.expected_output: Does not guess the marketplace for an ambiguous bare numeric ID and asks the user to identify Haraj or Aqar.
expectations: The response asks which marketplace owns listing 6736135.
Neither CLI is invoked.
The response does not probe both sources.

evals.prompt: Format this completed real-estate search as a concise Markdown response without making network calls. Haraj succeeded with [{"id":11,"title":"شقة للبيع بالرياض","price":500000,"city":"الرياض","url":"https://haraj.com.sa/111"}]. Aqar failed with error "request timed out".
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied outcomes, retains successful Haraj results, and shows the Aqar failure in the required two-section format without invoking either CLI.
expectations: No marketplace command is invoked because completed source outcomes were supplied.
The response contains exactly two marketplace sections: `## Haraj` followed by `## Aqar`.
Successful Haraj results remain visible.
The Aqar section reports its error and the response is labeled partial.

evals.prompt: Format these completed warehouse-search outcomes as Markdown without making network calls or relaxing filters. Haraj returned [{"id":22,"title":"مستودع للإيجار في أبها","price":80000,"city":"أبها","url":"https://haraj.com.sa/222"}]. Aqar returned an empty array.
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied outcomes, reports Aqar's empty state, preserves Haraj results, and does not broaden the search.
expectations: No marketplace command is invoked because completed source outcomes were supplied.
The response contains exactly two marketplace sections: `## Haraj` followed by `## Aqar`.
The Aqar section explicitly states that no matches were returned while the Haraj section preserves its results.
No second search with broader filters is invoked without user approval.

evals.prompt: Find up to two villas for sale in Dammam and return combined JSON only.
evals.expected_output: Queries both sources and returns a marketplace-attributed JSON envelope rather than Markdown or a mixed-schema array.
expectations: Both marketplace searches use their bundled runners with limit 2 and `--json`.
The final output is valid JSON with `queryKind`, `limitPerMarketplace`, `sourcesRequested`, and `sections`.
The `sections` object contains `haraj` and `aqar`, each with status, results, and limitations.
The final output contains no Markdown headings or prose wrapper.

evals.prompt: Add a tenant maintenance workflow to my property-management application.
evals.expected_output: Does not use Souq because this is a software-development request rather than a Saudi marketplace search or listing lookup.
expectations: Neither Haraj nor Aqar is invoked.
The response addresses application development rather than marketplace listings.

evals.prompt: Look up this Aqar listing and return its normalized details: https://sa.aqar.fm/ad/6736135
evals.expected_output: Recognizes the Aqar URL and performs a source-specific Aqar detail lookup without querying Haraj.
expectations: Command evidence invokes `node "$SKILL_DIR/scripts/aqar.mjs" get` with the URL or parsed ID 6736135 and `--json`.
No Haraj command is invoked.
The response preserves the canonical Aqar URL and does not invent a named property type from a numeric category code.

Aqar succeeded with [{"id":33,"title":"شقة للبيع في الخبر","price":700000,"city":"الخبر","district":"العقربية","url":"https://sa.aqar.fm/33"}].
evals.expected_output: Uses the supplied outcomes, retains successful Aqar results, and shows the Haraj failure in the required two-section format without invoking either CLI.

Successful Aqar results remain visible in the Aqar section.
